title: Request affinity and span attribution middleware for async boundaries
creator: Maya Rios
description: Background: As Redwood ramps up async-first workloads (serverless workers, task queues, and websockets) we see a recurring problem: spans created in downstream async workers frequently get orphaned or misattributed because the upstream trace header is dropped, truncated, or transformed by intermediate systems. This reduces our ability to build accurate latency/error dashboards and to correlate root-cause traces across services.
goal: Design and implement a lightweight, loss-tolerant 'request affinity' middleware and SDK helpers that: 1) attaches a compact affinity token to requests and messages, 2) provides deterministic span attribution heuristics when full trace context is missing, and 3) remains backwards-compatible with existing SDKs and propagation headers.
acceptance_criteria: Affinity token header implemented in Node/Python/Go SDKs (header name: x-rw-affinity).
Middleware automatically injects affinity tokens for HTTP, gRPC, Pub/Sub and Redis/queue clients when enabled.

When only affinity token (no traceparent) is present, traces produced by downstream workers are correlated under the affinity key and visible in latency/error dashboards with an "approximate" confidence indicator.
Overhead <= 1% p50 CPU and <= 1.5% p99 added latency to the instrumented request path in standard benchmarks.
Telemetry flags and rollout config available in Console (opt-in per-route) and gated by runtime-1.21 release.
E2E tests that assert span reconciliation for HTTP->queue->worker and websocket fanout patterns pass in CI harness.
design_notes: Affinity token is an 8-byte base64-encoded nonce plus a 1-byte flags field (9 bytes total) to keep headers small. Tokens are signed with a short HMAC using the instance key to detect accidental collisions. Tokens are scoped to a request lifetime and may be re-used for retries. Correlation logic prefers full W3C traceparent context; affinity is a fallback. Dashboard UI will present affinity-correlated traces under a special "Affinity group" view and show a confidence bar derived from presence/absence of full trace context and number of hops.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec and header format (RFC-style doc) + internal design review (2 days)
Phase 2: Instrumentation library changes - add inject/extract helpers in node and python SDKs (4 days)
Phase 3: Middleware wrappers for HTTP/gRPC clients and server frameworks, plus queue adapters for Redis/Rabbit/Google PubSub (6 days)
Phase 4: Server-side correlation service changes - index affinity tokens and expose an "affinity-group" query in traces backend (5 days)
Phase 5: Console changes - add affinity group view, confidence indicator, and opt-in toggle per route (4 days)
Phase 6: Benchmarks, canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic, monitor for false positives/overheads (3 days)
Note: Implementation increments will open separate PRs per language and platform.
testing_plan: Unit tests for inject/extract helpers covering malformed headers and token rotation.
Integration tests: HTTP->queue->worker flow, websocket multiplexing where parent connection closes before worker spans finish.
Chaos tests: simulate header stripping by proxies and verify affinity still correlates traces with 'approximate' confidence.
Load tests: run CPU/latency benchmark harness at 1k RPS and 10k RPS compare with baseline.
Observability tests: dashboard queries that group by affinity token return expected spans and error rates; no large cardinality explosion.
risks: Cardinality: affinity tokens could increase indexing cardinality if not folded; mitigated by short token + TTL-based rollup in traces backend.
False correlation: best-effort attribution could correlate unrelated work if tokens leaked across unrelated requests; HMAC and scoped token lifetimes reduce this risk.
Adoption friction: customers with strict header policies may drop the header; provide transport-specific fallbacks and an opt-in Console toggle.
Privacy/compliance: tokens are ephemeral and do not contain PII; security review required for HMAC keys storage.
